read.sections.0.text.note: Translator: "Skala dekat / skala luas" is used for close/wide scale. In geography, "skala besar/kecil" has a different technical meaning, so these were avoided. Check that "dekat/luas" reads naturally. Back-translation check: Translator flag stands: check that 'skala dekat / skala luas' (close / wide scale) reads naturally. 'Skala besar/kecil' was avoided on purpose because it has a technical meaning in geography.
read.sections.0.text.back: On a map on a screen, you can zoom in to see one street or zoom out to see the whole country. Historians do something similar with the past, because they choose a scale. Scale means how big the time period, place or group is that you choose to study. A close scale looks at one day, one letter or one family. A wide scale might follow a whole town for 100 years, or compare many regions over thousands of years. Look at Riverstone. At the scale of one afternoon, the story is about rain and a closed bridge. Over a period of 20 years, the story is about a growing town. Over a period of a few hundred years, the story is about a river that shifted.
read.sections.0.text.source: On a map on a screen, you can zoom in to see one street or zoom out to see a whole country. Historians do something similar with the past, because they choose a scale. Scale means how big a piece of time, place or group you decide to study. A close scale looks at one day, one letter or one family. A wide scale might follow a whole town for 100 years, or compare many regions over thousands of years. Look at Riverstone. At the scale of one afternoon, the story is about rain and a closed bridge. Over 20 years, it is about a town that grows. Over several hundred years, it is about a river that moves.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: On a map, you can zoom in and zoom out. Historians also do this with the past. They choose a scale. Scale means how much time or place you look at. A close scale is one day or one family. A wide scale is a town over 100 years. In Riverstone, the story of one afternoon is about rain and a bridge. In 20 years, the town grew. In hundreds of years, the river shifted.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: On a map, you can zoom in and out. Historians do this with the past too. They choose a scale. Scale means how much time or place you look at. A close scale is one day or one family. A wide scale is a town over 100 years. In Riverstone, the story of one afternoon is about rain and a bridge. Over 20 years, the town grows. read.sections.1.text.note: Back-translation check: 'bukti dekat' (close evidence) reads oddly. 'Bukti skala dekat' or 'bukti daripada pandangan dekat' may be clearer. The same applies to 'sumber dekat' in read.checks.1.options.2.feedback.
read.sections.1.text.back: A close view helps us notice people's choices, feelings and small details. A diary, a receipt or a photograph can show how an event changed someone's day. For example, a trader's diary might state that he/she waited six hours before the bridge was opened. However, one person's day is not necessarily the same as another person's day. Another trader might have taken the long road. Therefore, close evidence needs context, that is, we need to know what was happening around it at that time.
read.sections.1.text.source: A close view helps us notice people's choices, feelings and small details. A diary, a receipt or one photograph can show how an event changed one person's day. For example, a trader's diary might say that she waited six hours for the bridge to open. However, one person's day is not always the same as everyone else's. Other traders may have taken the long road instead. So close evidence needs context, which means we need to know what was happening around it at the time.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: A close view shows people. We see their choices and feelings. A diary or receipt shows a person's day. A trader might wait six hours for the bridge. But another trader might take the long road. One person's day is not everyone's day. So we need context. Context is what is happening around that source.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: A close view shows people. We see their choices and feelings. A diary or a receipt shows one person's day. A trader may wait six hours for the bridge. But other traders may take the long road. One person's day is not everyone's day. So we need context. Context is what is going on around the source.

read.sections.2.text.back: A wide view helps us see patterns, that is, changes that repeat or continue for a long time. Maps from many different years can show Riverstone slowly growing across the river. But a wide view can also hide people, because one line on a timeline cannot show every person's choices. Some historians zoom out as far as possible, all the way to the whole history of the universe. At that scale, a town is too small to be seen. That is why historians move between scales. No scale is always better, because the best scale depends on the question you ask.
read.sections.2.text.source: A wide view helps us see a pattern, which is a change that repeats or goes on for a long time. Maps from many different years can show Riverstone slowly spreading across the river. But a wide view can also hide people, because a line on a timeline cannot show every person's choices. Some historians zoom out as far as possible, to the whole history of the universe. At that scale, one town is far too small to see. That is why historians move between scales. Neither scale is always better, because the best scale depends on the question you ask.

read.sections.2.simpler.note: Back-translation check: Changed 'Ketika itu' (at that time) to 'Pada skala itu' (at that scale), which is what 'Then' means here.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: A wide view shows patterns. A pattern is a change that continues for a long time. Maps from many years show the town getting bigger. But a wide view can hide people. A timeline cannot show every person. Some historians look at the whole universe. At that time, you cannot see a town at all. So historians move from close to wide. The best scale depends on your question.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: A wide view shows a pattern. A pattern is a change that goes on for a long time. Maps from many years show the town getting bigger. But a wide view can hide people. A timeline cannot show every person. Some historians look at the whole universe. Then you cannot see one town at all. So historians move from close to wide. The best scale depends on your question.

write.example.back: At the scale of one afternoon, we notice heavy rain and a closed bridge. A trader had to take a longer road, so he/she arrived late. Over a period of 20 years, the evidence shows a town that is growing. New houses and markets spread to both sides of the river. A close scale helps us answer why a trader was late on that day. A wide scale helps us answer why Riverstone built two new bridges. Together, both scales show that one place can have more than one story.
write.example.source: At the scale of one afternoon, we notice heavy rain and a closed bridge. A trader has to take a longer road, so she arrives late. Over 20 years, the evidence shows a town that is growing. New homes and markets spread to both sides of the river. The close scale helps us answer why one trader was late that day. The wide scale helps us answer why Riverstone built two new bridges. Together, the two scales show that one place can have more than one story.

watch.summary.back: This short video uses the widest scale: the history of the whole universe. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, it was very small and very hot. Then it became bigger and cooler. Since then, it has kept changing. At this scale, you do not see a single person, a town or a country. You only see very big changes over billions of years. This helps us see that human history is a small part of a much longer story. But this scale cannot tell us why a trader was late, or how a family lived. To find out those things, historians zoom in.
watch.summary.source: This short video uses the widest scale there is: the history of the whole universe. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, it was very small and very hot. Then it grew bigger and cooler. It has kept changing ever since. At this scale, you do not see any person, town or country. You see only very big changes over billions of years. This helps us see that human history is a small part of a much longer story. But this scale cannot tell us why one trader was late, or how one family lived. To learn those things, historians zoom in.
